question.generalHint: 그 여성의 이름은 이즈모노 오쿠니로 전한다.

facts.claim: 1603년 이즈모 대사 무녀였을 수도 있는 오쿠니가 젊은 여성 무용수들과 가모강 마른 강바닥 임시 무대에서 공연
facts.note: The history of kabuki began in 1603 during the Edo period when former shrine maiden Izumo no Okuni, possibly a miko of Izumo-taisha, began performing with a troupe of young female dancers a new, simple style of dance drama in pantomime, on a makeshift stage in the dry bed of the Kamo River in Kyoto.
It did not take long for the style to become popular, and Okuni was asked to perform before the Imperial Court.

facts.claim: 1629년 여성 출연 금지 뒤 남성만, 여자 역 배우는 온나가타
facts.note: developed into its present all-male theatrical form after women were banned from performing in kabuki theatre in 1629 ... Cross-dressing male actors, known as "onnagata" (lit., "woman role") or "oyama" took over previously female- or wakashu-acted roles.

question.hintNote: is believed to have invented the theatrical art form of kabuki.
